title: The printing press
body:
Johannes Gutenberg developed a movable-type printing press in Mainz around 1440. His Bible, completed around 1455, was the first major book printed with metal movable type in Europe.

Printing spread quickly: by 1500 presses were operating in more than two hundred European towns. Cheaper books helped spread the ideas of the Renaissance and, after 1517, the pamphlets of the Protestant Reformation.

title: The Roman Republic
body:
Rome became a republic in 509 BC, when its last king was expelled and power passed to elected magistrates and the Senate. The republic expanded across Italy and, after the Punic Wars, around the Mediterranean.

Civil wars in the first century BC weakened republican institutions. Julius Caesar was assassinated in 44 BC, and in 27 BC Octavian took the title Augustus, beginning the Roman Empire.

title: The Industrial Revolution
body:
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the second half of the eighteenth century. James Watt patented his improved steam engine in 1769, and mechanised cotton mills spread through Lancashire in the following decades.

The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened in 1830 as the first inter-city line powered entirely by steam locomotives. By 1850 Britain had more than six thousand miles of railway, and industrialisation was spreading to Belgium, France, Germany, and the United States.

title: The First World War
body:
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in June 1914 set off a chain of declarations of war among the European powers. Trench warfare soon stalled the Western Front.

The United States entered the war in 1917. Fighting ended with the armistice of 11 November 1918, and the Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.

title: The Space Race
body:
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, in 1957. Yuri Gagarin became the first person to orbit the Earth in 1961.

The United States answered with the Apollo program, and in 1969 Apollo 11 landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon. The rivalry eased in 1975, when Apollo and Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit.

title: Magna Carta
body:
King John of England agreed to Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215 under pressure from rebellious barons. The charter limited royal power and promised protection from illegal imprisonment.

It was reissued several times, notably in 1225, and later became a symbol of the principle that the monarch is subject to the law.
